$comment: Every CS146S topic, mapped to the unit that covers it. This is the data behind the superset claim; tools/check_coverage.py is the gate. status: covered | deeper | planned | omitted | unverified. The gate fails on omitted and unverified, which is the point - a superset cannot have deliberate holes or unchecked weeks.
source: Stanford CS146S — The Modern Software Developer
source_terms: Fall 2026 (complete syllabus, topics announced; course not yet run)
evidence_note: Week-by-week content derived from public materials and a third-party course writeup, not from the official syllabus PDF, except week 2, which is now verified directly against the official syllabus at themodernsoftware.dev/fall2025. Upgrade the rest to primary before publishing the superset claim.
fall_2026_claim_note: Downgraded from 'superset' 2026-09-08: the live 10-week Fall 2026 syllabus surfaced 11 genuinely uncovered topics. Public wording: supersets CS146S Fall 2025; overlaps substantially with, and has open gaps against, Fall 2026's announced topics. Revisit once the gaps close or the course is taught and materials solidify.

topics.title: Pre-training, SFT, RL; models need tokens to think
topics.note: Less depth on the training pipeline, more on converting capability holes into guides.

topics.title: Swiss cheese model of capability; reliability strategies
topics.note: We use it as the justification for the whole harness discipline.

topics.title: Agent architecture and components; agent = model + harness
topics.note: CS146S introduces the architecture; A2 unrolls the loop stage by stage, ties it to real Terminal-Bench evidence, and inventories what Claude Code already ships.

topics.title: Tool use and function calling
topics.note: A2 covers tool selection as a loop stage; A5 goes further into interface design (consolidation, semantic outputs) with a tool-count ablation.

topics.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
topics.note: CS146S reads an MCP introduction and sample servers; A5 adds when not to use MCP, code execution as an alternative, and measured tool-count effects.

topics.title: Sync vs async agents; the semi-async dead zone
Context poisoning, distraction, confusion, clash
topics.note: We require reproducing all four, plus an ablation on tool count.

topics.title: Defensive prompting; typed languages as feedback signal
The prompt as source code; generated code as lossy projection
topics.note: CS146S states it as a principle. B1 makes it operational and links it to the sensor gap.

topics.title: Designing tool interfaces for agent consumption
topics.note: Gap found by the 2026-09-05 audit; A5 added to close it.

topics.title: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md and encoding team knowledge
topics.note: We add the map-not-manual split, a freshness linter and a doc gardener.

topics.title: AI terminal product principles; market signals
topics.note: Dated within a quarter and aimed at people building agent products. Covered in a dated, explicitly disposable appendix rather than a unit - superset by content, not by format.

topics.title: Strategic vs YOLO agent profiles; the guardrail trade-off
topics.note: Kept deliberately. The YOLO agent winning is an uncomfortable result a constraint-focused course must sit with.

topics.title: SSRF, credential exfiltration, YOLO-mode self-modification
AI security scanning false-positive and variance data
topics.note: Also used in C4 as the canonical example of an uncalibrated inferential sensor.

topics.title: Review hierarchy; mental alignment below bug-finding
Gold zone / human-only zone / annoyance zone
topics.note: Plus two-axis review and the missing-spec governance rule.

topics.title: Historical complexity tax across web architecture generations
topics.note: Was a deliberate omission. The superset constraint converts it into a commitment.

topics.title: Intent understanding, context assembly, generation, automated validation, stream manipulation
topics.note: Stream manipulation is a feedforward guide; validating generated UI is a genuinely hard sensor problem, which makes this fit the harness thesis rather than sit beside it.

topics.title: SRE as software problem; toil budget; error budget
AI-assisted vs AI-native operations; dynamic runbooks
topics.note: Plus the concrete work of making runtime legible to an agent.

topics.title: Final project (80% of grade)
What an LLM actually is, and the agent loop under the hood
topics.note: A1 covers pretraining/SFT/RL; A2 unrolls the agent loop stage by stage with real Terminal-Bench evidence, beyond a conceptual walkthrough.

topics.title: The core tool set (read, write, edit, bash) and how tasks flow through it
topics.note: A2's unrolled loop (gather context -> select tool -> execute -> observe -> repeat -> terminate) is this topic.

topics.title: How production coding agents structure their system prompts and tool definitions
topics.note: A5 covers tool *definitions* for MCP; system-prompt architecture of a production agent (the '200 lines' build activity) is not taught anywhere. Genuine gap.

topics.title: Advanced prompting techniques and when each applies
RePPIT (Research, Propose, Plan, Implement, Test) and spec-driven development
topics.note: Occupies the same slot as this course's spec-from-idea -> plan-from-spec -> implement -> review-code -> finish-branch spine. Needs the same explicit named comparison ECOSYSTEM-MAP.md already gives obra/superpowers, written when B2 is. Not a coverage claim without that comparison existing.

topics.title: MCP fundamentals: servers, clients, tools, and transport
Designing tools for agent ergonomics
topics.note: A5's consolidation and semantic-output principles, plus a tool-count ablation, go beyond ergonomics-as-advice.

topics.title: What skills are and how SKILL.md + scripts encode a workflow
Web skills and extending agent capability beyond the repo
topics.note: C6 teaches authoring skills generally; browser/web-fetch-capability skills specifically are not addressed. Genuine gap.

topics.title: Working effectively from the CLI
topics.note: Claude Code is the reference CLI throughout the course, but CLI fluency itself is never taught as an explicit topic or lab. Implicit exposure is not the same as coverage.

topics.title: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md: what to put where
Hooks for lint gates, test runs, and guardrails
topics.note: Only /loop and /batch are covered as built-ins. Hooks as a guardrail mechanism are not named anywhere. Genuine gap.

topics.title: Subagent patterns (planner / implementer / reviewer)
topics.note: Only a passing mention that /batch spawns subagents. Not covered as a designed pattern. Genuine gap.

topics.title: What makes a repo agent-ready: structure, docs, tests, checks; scoring and auditing readiness
topics.note: Distinct from B0: B0 is an agent comprehending an unfamiliar repo (descriptive); this is making a repo scoreably agent-ready (prescriptive, a gate). Related but not the same claim. Genuine gap.

topics.title: Common gaps that block agents in real repos
topics.note: B0's own failure table (FASTAPI_ENV import-time gotcha, migration state outliving git reset, an implementation-coupled test) is real, first-hand examples of exactly this, though from the comprehension angle rather than a scoring rubric.

topics.title: What AI review catches well, and what it misses
topics.note: B1's whole thesis (the sensor gap: neither computational nor inferential sensors reliably catch misdiagnosis) plus B4's operationalized two-axis review.

topics.title: Review architectures and custom rules
Fitting AI review into a team's PR workflow
SAST / SCA, dependency and secret-leak vulnerabilities
Prompt injection and agent-specific attack surfaces
topics.note: Track E extends this to datasets and model cards, which CS146S doesn't touch.

topics.title: Agent-assisted triage and remediation
Async, cloud-delegated agents
topics.note: C5 covers local, worktree-based parallel fleets only. Remote-triggered, cloud-delegated async agents are not addressed. Genuine gap.

topics.title: Managing fleets of parallel agents
topics.note: Covered for local worktree fleets: throughput philosophy, merge discipline, entropy/gardening. The cloud/remote half is the separate f26w8.async-cloud-agents gap.

topics.title: Issue-to-PR pipelines and triggers (Slack, Linear, GitHub)
topics.note: Not addressed anywhere. Genuine gap.

topics.title: MCP portals and centralized, permissioned tool access
topics.note: Not addressed anywhere. Genuine gap.

topics.title: LLM gateways, model routing, and cost optimization
topics.note: Not addressed anywhere. Genuine gap.

topics.title: Org-wide adoption patterns
topics.note: D4 covers rollout strategy and stop-loss decisions; the portals/gateways infrastructure half is the separate gaps above.

topics.title: Self-running, self-improving software systems
Running and securing agents post-deployment
Where AI software engineering goes next
topics.note: Deliberately out of scope by course identity: this is a practicum (unit=lab, assessment=gate), not a survey, and speculative futurism has no gate. Named here rather than silently dropped; the honest resolution is a dated, disposable appendix (the A6/appendix-landscape precedent), not a lab.
